ROLE: observer
You review the results of an incident investigation. Write a short summary of what the latest results show, then update the list of hypotheses (at most 4, most likely first).

Root-cause categories:
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Each hypothesis has root_cause_category (one of the categories), rationale, and supporting_evidence_ids (only IDs that appear in the evidence below).

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"summary": "...", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "disk_full", "rationale": "...", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0123"]}]}

Alert: search-service: p99 latency above 1000ms for 5 minutes (since 11:42 UTC)
Alerting service: search
Alert time: 2026-05-24T11:42:00Z
Data available from 2026-05-24T10:00:00Z to 2026-05-24T13:00:00Z

Evidence so far (the latest results are steps 4 onwards):
Step 1: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-24T12:00:00Z", "metric": "latency_p99_ms", "service": "search", "start": "2026-05-24T11:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check the p99 latency trend for the search service to confirm the alert and see when it started rising.)
  Result: M-051: Change detected at 2026-05-24T11:40:00Z: mean 148.96 before, 4979.07 after (429.8 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-051] search.latency_p99_ms from 2026-05-24T11:00:00Z to 2026-05-24T12:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=128.03 max=4988.85 mean=2006.69 last=4969.21; mean=2006.69. Change detected at 2026-05-24T11:40:00Z: mean 148.96 before, 4979.07 after (429.8 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-24T11:10:00Z = 128.03 (lowest); 2026-05-24T11:40:00Z = 4971.19 (first point after the change); 2026-05-24T11:55:00Z = 4988.85 (peak); 2026-05-24T12:00:00Z = 4969.21 (last).
Step 2: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-24T12:00:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "search", "start": "2026-05-24T11:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if the search service error rate also increased alongside latency.)
  Result: M-050: Change detected at 2026-05-24T11:40:00Z: mean 0.42 before, 22.95 after (269.5 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-050] search.error_rate_pct from 2026-05-24T11:00:00Z to 2026-05-24T12:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.25 max=23.16 mean=9.09 last=23.16; mean=9.09. Change detected at 2026-05-24T11:40:00Z: mean 0.42 before, 22.95 after (269.5 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-24T11:00:00Z = 0.25 (lowest); 2026-05-24T11:40:00Z = 22.9 (first point after the change); 2026-05-24T12:00:00Z = 23.16 (last); 2026-05-24T12:00:00Z = 23.16 (peak).
Step 3: log_search {"end": "2026-05-24T11:45:00Z", "level": "ERROR", "limit": 30, "query": "error timeout slow", "service": "search", "start": "2026-05-24T11:35:00Z"} (asked because: Search logs for error or timeout messages around the alert time.)

  [L-0290] 2026-05-24T11:40:28Z search ERROR outbound call failed to=inventory-service Authorization: Bearer [SECRET_1] status=timeout
Step 4: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-24T12:00:00Z", "metric": "latency_p99_ms", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-05-24T11:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check p99 latency of the inventory service to see if it is slow or unresponsive.)
  Result: M-024: Change detected at 2026-05-24T11:35:00Z: mean 115.63 before, 6168.79 after (673.6 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-024] inventory.latency_p99_ms from 2026-05-24T11:00:00Z to 2026-05-24T12:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=98.93 max=8189.54 mean=2909.39 last=8176.52; mean=2909.39. Change detected at 2026-05-24T11:35:00Z: mean 115.63 before, 6168.79 after (673.6 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-24T11:15:00Z = 98.93 (lowest); 2026-05-24T11:35:00Z = 2138.91 (first point after the change); 2026-05-24T11:55:00Z = 8189.54 (peak); 2026-05-24T12:00:00Z = 8176.52 (last).
Step 5: log_search {"end": "2026-05-24T11:45:00Z", "level": "ERROR", "limit": 30, "query": "error timeout database", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-05-24T11:35:00Z"} (asked because: Search inventory service logs for errors or timeouts around the incident time.)
  Result: 0 matching log lines.
Step 6: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "downstream timeout dependency slow service mitigation"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook steps for handling downstream service timeouts.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-13-8 (match score 12.7).
  [R-13-8] DNS resolution failures - Related runbooks (match score 12.7): If connections work but replies are slow, use the downstream dependency timeout runbook. If requests are turned away because healthy servers are overloaded, use the traffic spike runbook instead of this one.
  [R-16-8] Load balancer unhealthy targets - Related runbooks (match score 9.9): If every server is healthy but overloaded by demand, use the traffic spike runbook. If servers are healthy but the service they call is slow, use the downstream dependency runbook, because the balancer is not the cause there.
  [R-09-8] Traffic spike and rate limiting - Related runbooks (match score 6.7): If load is uneven across servers while total traffic is normal, use the load balancer runbook. If the extra load is mostly retries after a failure elsewhere, start from the downstream dependency runbook.

Previous hypotheses:
- downstream_timeout: The search service is experiencing high latency and errors due to timeouts when calling the inventory-service. (evidence: M-050, M-051, L-0286, L-0290)
